svg.title: How the memory planner reuses GPU buffers
svg.desc: The same example network is shown as in the Engine construction diagram, with symbolic shape [b, h, w, c]. Cube marks are tensors and chip marks are GPU buffers. The planner first merges view aliases and classifies GPU-required storage. Temporary Tensor 1 is produced by Conv at operation 0 and last read by ReLU 1 at operation 1. Tensor 2 lives from ReLU 1 at 1 through Add at 2. Tensor 3 lives from Add at 2 through ReLU 2 at 3. Tensor 1 and Tensor 3 may share Buffer 2 because 1 is strictly less than 2, provided the capacity fits. Tensor 2 and Tensor 3 cannot share because Add reads Tensor 2 while writing Tensor 3: 2 is not less than 2. Process storage groups in order of first write, choosing the smallest nonpersistent slot whose previous last use is strictly before the next first write and whose capacity is sufficient, or create a new slot if none fits. The packed timeline shows Tensor 1 and Tensor 3 in Buffer 2 and Tensor 2 in Buffer 3. A branch extends lifetime to the latest consumer. Reshape aliases merge into one root and a lifetime covering all consumers; Tensor 4 and output share Buffer 4. Input, output alias groups, and GPU constants reserve persistent slots. Weights used only to build layers and CPU-only shape parameters receive no graph slot. MemoryPlan contains slots, tensor_slots, and constants, and creates no Vulkan objects. AllocateVulkanBuffers subsequently creates one buffer per slot and binds tensors using shared ownership. Inference overwrites reused storage after the last read, with command barriers and no graph-buffer allocation or freeing per operation. Buffer numbers are illustrative and lifetimes are logical operation positions rather than wall-clock time.
svg.text: Identify GPU data in the graph
Weights → layer-owned buffers. Shape → CPU only. Neither needs a graph buffer here.
Compute lifetimes: first write → last GPU read
Track every consumer; interval endpoints count.
Add reads one while writing the other.
Tensor 1 is dead before Add; Tensor 2 is still needed by Add.
Pack lifetimes into the smallest eligible slots
Process groups by first write. Reuse only nonpersistent slots with:
3 temporary tensors → 2 reusable slots. No GPU allocation yet.
Keep storage safe: branches, aliases, persistent data
One root; include all alias consumers.
Output view reserves the entire group.
Allocate once, then reuse during inference
Static bindings + GPU barriers; no per-op graph-buffer allocation or freeing.
Buffer IDs are schematic. Timeline positions are operation indices, not elapsed time.
